content:
I tried to set up the lean4 dev environment on a windows machine today, and hit an issue where the stage0 dlls couldn't be found. Claude suggested that this was because they wind up in bin on windows rather than lib/lean, making the following change to src/lakefile.toml.in:

--- a/src/lakefile.toml.in
+++ b/src/lakefile.toml.in
@@ -77,4 +77,4 @@
 # Load the previous stage's lake native code into lake's build process in order to prevent ABI
 # breakages from affecting bootstrapping.
-moreLeanArgs = ["--plugin", "${PREV_STAGE}/lib/lean/libLake_shared${CMAKE_SHARED_LIBRARY_SUFFIX}"]
+moreLeanArgs = ["--plugin", "${PREV_STAGE}/${CMAKE_RELATIVE_LIBRARY_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY}/libLake_shared${CMAKE_SHARED_LIBRARY_SUFFIX}"]

and then the local build succeeded.

(Note: this is with a fresh msys2 and cmake install.)

Is this a reasonable change? Or did I do something incorrectly to get here?
I've confirmed, I (had an agent) went throught the dev instructions on a fresh windows VM, and hit exactly the same problem.
@Thomas Murrills, could you open an issue? I'll ask Mac/Sebastian about it and we can decide if this is the right fix, and if this is a blocker for the next release.
